title: Classic Hawaiian Ahi Tuna Poke with Sesame, Macadamia and Rice
summary: Cubes of raw yellowfin tuna in a soy, sesame and ginger dressing with onion, spring onion and toasted macadamias, piled over short-grain rice with sesame and nori.

ingredients.item: red or sweet onion, very thinly sliced
spring onions, whites and greens sliced separately
unsalted macadamia nuts, toasted and chopped
nori sheet, snipped into thin strips

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs nearly clear, then boil it with 360 ml water, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 min. Rest it off the heat for 10 min, fluff and let it cool until just warm, so it does not cook the fish.

steps.title: Mix the dressing
steps.text: Whisk together the soy sauce, neutral oil, sesame oil, ginger, garlic and chilli flakes in a small bowl. Taste it on its own; it should be salty, nutty and gently hot.

steps.title: Toast the nuts
steps.text: Shake the macadamias in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 3-4 min until golden in patches and fragrant. Cool, then chop roughly; toasting brings out their buttery taste and keeps them crunchy.

steps.title: Dress the tuna
steps.text: No more than 15 min before eating, fold the tuna cubes through the dressing with the onion, spring onion whites and half the nuts. Chill for 5-10 min; any longer and the salt starts to firm the fish and draw out its juices.

steps.title: Build the bowls
steps.text: Spoon the rice into four bowls and top with the poke and its dressing. Scatter over the spring onion greens, the rest of the nuts, the sesame seeds and strips of nori, and eat at once.

tips: Cut the tuna with a sharp knife on a cold board and keep the cubes even, so every piece takes up the dressing at the same speed.
Add diced avocado or cucumber for a creamier, fresher bowl.
A common mistake is dressing the tuna hours ahead; it turns grey and mushy.
safety: RAW NOTE: the fish is eaten raw. Buy sushi- or sashimi-grade fish from a fishmonger you trust that has been frozen first (-20 °C for 7 days or -35 °C for 15 hours), keep it in the fridge until the last minute and eat it the same day. Pregnant people, young children, older adults and anyone with weakened immunity should skip it.
storage: Poke is best eaten straight away. Leftover dressed tuna should be discarded; plain rice keeps 1 day in the fridge (cool it quickly). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
